chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever has a newborn child, let him recite the Adhan (call to prayer) in his right ear with the Adhan of the Prayer, and let him recite the Iqamah in the left, for it is a safeguarding from the Pelted Satan.'

key_terms.أَذَان: Adhan: The call to prayer, recited in the newborn's right ear.
key_terms.إِقَامَة: Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited in the newborn's left ear.
key_terms.الشَّيْطَان الرَّجِيم: Al-Shaytan Al-Rajim: The Pelted Satan, from whom the child is protected.
key_terms.عِصْمَة: Ismah: Protection or safeguarding from evil influences.

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in a newborn's ears according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of reciting the Adhan in the right ear and Iqamah in the left for newborns, a practice rooted in the belief that it implants the call to prayer in the child's soul to ward off Shaytan. In Shia scholarship, this ritual is viewed as an initial spiritual imprinting (Tajalli) of divine guidance, ensuring the child's first auditory experiences are anchored in Tawhid. It reflects the broader theological concept of the soul's covenant with God, manifesting physically through the ears.
